blocks.text: Did you know that the same element, carbon, can form both the hardest natural substance on Earth and a soft lubricant?

blocks.markdown: Carbon is a unique element that can exist in different forms known as allotropes. These allotropes have distinct physical properties due to differences in their atomic arrangements.

blocks.title: Allotropy
blocks.text: Allotropy is the existence of an element in more than one form in the same physical state. Carbon's allotropes include diamond, graphite, and amorphous carbon.

blocks.markdown: The structure of each allotrope determines its properties. Diamond has a three-dimensional tetrahedral structure, making it extremely hard. Graphite, on the other hand, has a layered structure with weak forces between the layers, allowing them to slide over each other easily.

blocks.title: Properties of Diamond and Graphite
blocks.prompt: Explain why diamond is hard and graphite is soft.

steps.text: Diamond has a tetrahedral structure where each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four other carbon atoms, forming a rigid three-dimensional network.
Graphite consists of layers of carbon atoms arranged in hexagonal rings. The layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide over each other.

blocks.answer: Diamond is hard due to its strong covalent bonds in a 3D network, while graphite is soft because its layers can slide over each other.

blocks.markdown: Amorphous carbon, such as charcoal, lacks a crystalline structure and is used for filtration and as a fuel.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that the properties of carbon allotropes are directly related to their structures. This is a common exam question!

points: Allotropy is the existence of an element in multiple forms in the same physical state.
Diamond, graphite, and amorphous carbon are the main allotropes of carbon.
